t19: The secret of task games isn't the task's difficulty, it's the timing. A hard task at the wrong moment freezes the group; tasks given at the right time become the night's most memorable part. The 20 ideas below are sorted into three tiers, from easy to hard.
t21: Show your last phone photo to the group.
t22: Describe the person next to you in three words.
t23: Hum the last song you listened to, the group guesses.
t25: Pick the most organized person in the group and say why.
t26: Say a sentence in an accent.
t27: Describe the phone wallpaper of the person to your right.
t28: Tier 2 — Performance tasks (if the room is warm)
t29: Explain a movie with gestures and expressions in 30 seconds.
t30: Silent movie: keep going until someone guesses.
t31: Read an ad slogan like a drama scene.
t32: Impersonate someone in the group until they're recognized.
t33: Do a 20-second stand-up bit with an object in your hand.
t34: Explain a song's chorus without words, just rhythm.
t35: Show three different emotions on your face in one minute.
t36: Tasks are scaled from easy to hard based on the square's point value; can be swapped with a joker, and timed tasks auto-countdown.
t37: Tier 3 — Group tasks (when the night peaks)
t38: As a group, choreograph a 10-second dance.
t39: Everyone adds a sentence to the same story, taking turns.
t40: In two teams, do a silent movie duel.
t41: Take the group's photo in five different poses.
t42: Everyone impersonate the person next to them.
t43: Sing a common song together in a whisper.
t46: A task done unwillingly chills the group; leave room to pass.
t48: A task with no time limit drags and loses its humor.
t50: The hardest task shouldn't come in the first half hour.
t52: Instead of reading the task list by hand, having the game distribute it prevents arguments and keeps the surprise. In Roll or Dare, when you roll, the task comes from the square's point value and the score registers automatically; you choose before the game which categories (Family, Party, Dare 18+) are open. Like the ideas above, you can write your own tasks and add them to the pool.
t54: Should task games have a pass right?
t55: Yes. Giving everyone at least one pass throughout the game prevents reluctant participation and tension. A player using a pass doesn't get that round's points—that's balance enough.
t57: Start increasing difficulty after the middle of the night. Relaxing the group with warmup tasks in early rounds significantly raises the acceptance rate of harder tasks later.
t58: How many tasks should I prepare?
t59: Three times the number of players in tasks carries a whole night without a repetition feeling. Using an app with a ready-made task pool removes this prep.
